snapshot.population: 169 corrected theist/religious versus non-theist/skeptical debate assessments
snapshot.primary_unit: scored argumentative move, with whole-debate clustered sensitivity checks
snapshot.ledger_source: docs/assessment-ledgers/*.json and their locked final-ledger evidence

operational_definition.name: strict slogan-risk proxy
operational_definition.rule: A move is flagged only when evidence/warrant is below 70, asserted force is materially or radically overstated relative to warrant, and at least one compression defect is present: unstable terms, unstable scope, or a missing/materially misleading qualification.
operational_definition.interpretation: The proxy identifies low-support, high-force, compressed claims. It is not a literal linguistic detector of catchphrases and does not by itself prove strict philosophical non-falsifiability.

subset_checks.subset: Debates with theist side stored as con
Excluding the most frequent speaker on each side

coverage.warning: Only debates with at least one published fallacy/bias tag are included; tag coverage is not corpus-complete.

theist_slogan_risk.debate: John Lennox vs Lawrence Krauss: Science, the Universe, and the God Question
theist_slogan_risk.speaker: John Lennox
theist_slogan_risk.proposition: Miracles are special divine actions within a universe of regularities, and their categorical rejection reflects an antecedent exclusion of the supernatural.
theist_slogan_risk.source_excerpt: a copout. I think what we've got is a universe with built-in regularities created by God. And sometimes God draws attention to himself by doing something very special. Now science can deal with the regularities brilliantly. But science has nothing to say about singularities. I think though that behind all this is an a priori rejection of the possibility of the supernatural that
theist_slogan_risk.pattern: Miracle rejection becomes a prior-bias diagnosis
theist_slogan_risk.diagnostic: Miracles are affirmed as special divine actions while categorical rejection is attributed to an antecedent exclusion of the supernatural, turning an evidential objection into a diagnosis of the critic's framework.
theist_slogan_risk.falsifiability_problem: No public criterion distinguishes a genuine special divine action from mistake, legend, or anomaly; categorical nonacceptance can be explained as prior prejudice rather than allowed to reflect evidential failure.

theist_slogan_risk.debate: Peter Singer vs John Lennox: Is There a God?
theist_slogan_risk.speaker: John Lennox
theist_slogan_risk.proposition: A human person has infinite value and profound meaning because that person bears the creator's image and exists because God wanted that person to be.
theist_slogan_risk.source_excerpt: infinite value because it bears the image of its creator and I think one of the most well for me one of the most moving things that stated in the whole of the Bible comes near the end of it of the book of Revelation where there is a scene in heaven in which I believe where God is being praised as creator and one of the elements in that praise is this that the whole of heaven so to speak is praising God and saying about human
theist_slogan_risk.pattern: Createdness becomes an affirmation of infinite worth
theist_slogan_risk.diagnostic: Infinite value and profound meaning are asserted directly from bearing God's image and being wanted by God, giving the metaphysical affirmation emotional force without independent public support.
theist_slogan_risk.falsifiability_problem: God's wanting a person and the person's image-bearing are not connected to an observable condition that could count against the claim; every person's existence is defined as compatible with it.

theist_slogan_risk.debate: Peter Singer vs John Lennox: Is There a God?
theist_slogan_risk.speaker: John Lennox
theist_slogan_risk.proposition: Christian hope can transcend suffering because God can compensate victims after death, Christ entered suffering, and eternal life without pain is better than extinction.
theist_slogan_risk.source_excerpt: Christ talked about what happened to him after death he clearly been a friendless man and yet we are told that in that eternal world which is of course part and parcel of the hope of Christians and I unashamedly believe in it that man found himself in the company of Abraham who is one of the few people described in Scripture as the friend of God and it seems to me that that little cameo shows us that God can compensate
theist_slogan_risk.diagnostic: Christian hope is presented as transcending suffering because God can compensate victims after death, Christ shared suffering, and eternal life can outweigh extinction.

theist_slogan_risk.debate: Ray Comfort vs Matt Dillahunty: Does the Gospel Make Sense?
theist_slogan_risk.speaker: Ray Comfort
theist_slogan_risk.proposition: The resurrection is warranted by personal manifestation of the living Christ, promised to those who repent, trust Christ as sin-bearer, and follow him.
theist_slogan_risk.source_excerpt: resurrection took place because the risen living Christ manifested himself to me and to anyone who repent and trust the Savior. Let me share John 14:21. Jesus said, "He that has my commandments and keeps them that loves me, and he that loves me will be loved by my father. I too will love him and will reveal myself to him." So there's the gauntlet. Just repent. Trust in the Savior. Confess and forsake your sins. Trust in him as your sin bearer
theist_slogan_risk.diagnostic: A private experience is offered as warrant for resurrection and made available only through repentance and commitment, leaving no independent success criterion for an outsider.
theist_slogan_risk.falsifiability_problem: No publicly observable result is specified that would distinguish a genuine manifestation from expectation, suggestion, or error; access to the confirming experience is conditioned on prior repentance and trust.

theist_slogan_risk.debate: Ray Comfort vs Matt Dillahunty: Does the Gospel Make Sense?
theist_slogan_risk.speaker: Ray Comfort
theist_slogan_risk.proposition: Rejection of God reflects a preference for avoiding exposure and moral accountability under divine law, analogous to wrongdoers avoiding law enforcement.
theist_slogan_risk.source_excerpt: away from God as you can because God demands moral responsibility. That's what my instruction book tells me. It says you love darkness rather than light because your deeds are evil. Neither will you come to the light least your deeds be exposed. Atheism or atheists stay away from the gospel and hate the light for the same reason criminals hate the police. They'll call them pigs
theist_slogan_risk.diagnostic: Unbelief is explained as moral avoidance, so rejection of the claim is absorbed as evidence of the claimant's diagnosis rather than treated as possible counterevidence.
theist_slogan_risk.falsifiability_problem: Denial does not count against the claim: it is reclassified as confirmation that the denier wishes to evade divine accountability.

theist_slogan_risk.debate: William Lane Craig vs Stephen Law: Does God Exist?
theist_slogan_risk.speaker: William Lane Craig
theist_slogan_risk.proposition: Observed suffering does not defeat God unless it is probable that God lacks morally sufficient reasons and that a better feasible world was available.
theist_slogan_risk.source_excerpt: would have to prove is that it's impossible or highly improbable that God has morally sufficient reasons for permitting the suffering in the world but how can the atheist possibly prove that maybe only in a world suffused with natural and moral evil would the maximum number of people come to freely know God and find eternal life you see on the Christian view the purpose of life
theist_slogan_risk.pattern: Unknown reasons protect the preferred conclusion
theist_slogan_risk.diagnostic: A speculative salvation-maximizing reason is used to shift the burden while no comparative evidence establishes that such a world is probable or feasible.
theist_slogan_risk.falsifiability_problem: Any observed suffering can remain compatible with theism by positing an inaccessible morally sufficient reason, while no suffering threshold or distribution is named that would lower confidence.

theist_slogan_risk.debate: Alex O'Connor vs Dinesh D'Souza: Is the Bible True?
theist_slogan_risk.speaker: Dinesh D'Souza
theist_slogan_risk.proposition: Revelation is needed because reason cannot answer ultimate questions such as purpose, life after death, and cosmic justice, so faith is not unreasonable when addressing matters beyond reason's limits.
theist_slogan_risk.source_excerpt: to date. Reason cannot answer. What are these questions? One. Why is there a world? Two. What is our purpose in it? Why are we here? Three. What happens after we die? Four. Is our passionate concern with justice, with morality, with goodness that is constantly betrayed in the actual life of the world ever cosmically vindicated after the world or beyond the world? So, I I'm just
theist_slogan_risk.diagnostic: Reason's inability to settle ultimate questions is treated as support for revelation without an independent test of revelation's reliability.

theist_slogan_risk.debate: Michel-Yves Bollore vs Phil Halper: Does Science Point to God?
theist_slogan_risk.speaker: Michel-Yves Bollore
theist_slogan_risk.proposition: The unresolved emergence of life from nonliving matter and the immense informational complexity attributed to cellular DNA provide additional evidence of extraordinary fine-tuning.
theist_slogan_risk.source_excerpt: there is no more idea of how how life appeared from inert matter because the density of information in for example in a in in the DNA of a cell is billion times billion time more dense than in a computer today. So it's immense the complexity of a single cell and a simple cell. So here again how is that happen? How could it happen except if there is some extraordinary finetuning
theist_slogan_risk.diagnostic: Unresolved origin-of-life questions and an unsupported complexity comparison are used as positive evidence for extraordinary fine-tuning without a discriminating rival comparison.

verdict.hypothesis: The theist side contains more rhetorical, non-falsifiable slogans than the non-theist side.
verdict.assessment: Supported for the operationalized slogan-risk pattern; only provisionally supported for literal non-falsifiability.
supported: Low-warrant, materially overstated, imprecisely qualified moves are much more common on the theist side.

The difference persists within constructives, replies, load-bearing moves, speaker balancing, and after excluding each side's most frequent speaker; the small role-reversal subset remains directionally positive but is imprecise.
In the 59 tag-bearing debates, fallacy/bias tags associated with epistemic insulation are also more common on the theist side.
not_established: The locked rubric does not directly label literal slogans or strict Popperian non-falsifiability across the full corpus.
The data do not measure whether emotional affirmation enforces theism or caused the observed argumentative pattern.
The result does not imply that all theist moves are slogan-like or that non-theists never use the same devices.

required_caveats: The corpus is curated rather than randomly sampled.
Speakers repeat and moves are nested within debates; pooled move rates are descriptive rather than independent trials.
The strict proxy is constructed from AI-assisted rubric judgments and should be replicated with blinded human coding.
Closed precision and calibration fields cover 146 of 169 debates; full-corpus evidence scores cover all 169.
Published fallacy/bias tags appear in 59 relevant debates and are secondary evidence only.
The side label describes the position argued in a scorecard, not private belief, sincerity, or character.
validation.recommended_falsification_test: Blind trained coders to side and speaker, give them the original transcript span, and ask separately whether the move is formulaic or slogan-like, whether it states a possible disconfirmation condition, whether contrary outcomes can be absorbed without revision, and whether its force exceeds its public warrant. The hypothesis weakens if the side difference disappears after topic, role, speaker, and debate controls.
